title: 'Pharma package': Council adopts new rules for a fairer and more competitive EU pharmaceutical sector
key_claim: The Council adopted the pharma package on 28 September 2026: EU countries will be able to require companies to supply protected medicines, and the regulation and directive still need adoption by the European Parliament.
frame_summary: Presents the package as a balance of eight-year data protection and an eleven-year cap with a new power for member states to require supply, and notes that Parliament must still adopt the texts.
verbatim_quote: EU countries will have the power to require pharmaceutical companies to supply medicines
verbatim_list: The regulation and directive that make up the pharma package now need to be adopted by the European Parliament.

title: Global Benchmark for Efficient Drug Pricing (GLOBE) Model
key_claim: The final GLOBE rule is effective on 30 November 2026, requires mandatory participation by manufacturers of GLOBE Model drugs, sets rebates against a benchmark based on international drug prices from a reference-country list that includes Germany, France, Italy and Spain, and runs performance years from 1 April 2027 to 31 March 2032.
frame_summary: Finalises a mandatory Medicare Part B model in which manufacturers pay rebates when US prices exceed a benchmark drawn from prices in listed reference countries.

title: The Lancet: New US Medicare pricing policies could reshape global pharmaceutical markets
key_claim: A Lancet modelling study of 195 patented medicines ($87.9 billion of Medicare annual spending) finds that for about 73% of the 138 with comparable reference data (101 of 138) the estimated cut exceeds the medicine's entire annual sales in the reference country, which could push manufacturers to raise prices or delay launches. Analyst arithmetic: the 37 medicines shown as within local sales are 138 minus 101.
frame_summary: Argues that US reference pricing makes low prices in reference countries so costly to manufacturers that raising prices or delaying launches becomes a rational response.

title: Time to rethink your operating model (EU pharmaceutical reform)
key_claim: The Council vote passed with 26 member states in favour and none against; application is expected around 2028 after a transitional period, and redesigning an operating model typically takes up to 12 months.
frame_summary: Tells pharmaceutical operators that the adopted EU package will apply around 2028 and that rebuilding their operating model takes up to a year, so preparation should start now.

title: CMS finalizes mandatory GLOBE Model implementing most-favored-nation drug pricing in Medicare Part B
key_claim: Participation stays mandatory, but CMS will waive it for manufacturers in the voluntary GENEROUS Model, cutting the estimated eligible manufacturers from 19 to 4, and will exclude orphan-only drugs, plasma-derived products and certain cell and gene therapies.
frame_summary: Reads the final rule as keeping mandatory participation while narrowing its reach through a GENEROUS waiver and product exclusions.

title: How long are patients WAITing for new treatments?
key_claim: The mean time from central marketing authorisation to country availability is 607 days across 36 countries, up from 509 days in 2019; the proposed EU obligation to launch on request carries loss of market exclusivity as the penalty. Analyst note: 607 days is the OHE mean and EFPIA's figure of 597 days is a separate quoted statement.
frame_summary: Argues that delay is driven by several factors, including company submission choices and national processes, and that a launch obligation is only one of them.

title: US push to cut drug prices could mean longer waits for European patients
key_claim: Under the updated EU rules a company must launch a new medicine within three years if a country requests it or lose two years of monopoly rights; Reuters reported that EU launches fell by some 35% in the ten months after the US executive order.
frame_summary: Warns that US price-cutting policy could lengthen waits for European patients and presents the EU launch duty as a counterweight whose effect may be limited.

title: 'United, we set the terms': Parliament pushes Europe to stand up to US drug pricing
key_claim: The Parliament health committee votes its second-reading recommendation on 10 November; the US Trade Representative opened a Section 301 investigation into Germany on 18 June 2026; patients already wait nearly 600 days on average between approval and access, in EFPIA's words.
